_comment: Source of truth for statements. Adding, removing or rewording any statement changes the statements version, which marks every audit stale until it is re-run (scripts/validate.js lists them). The agree/disagree/note/icon fields explain each statement to test takers and do not affect the statements version.

statements.text: The government should provide universal healthcare.
statements.agree: Everyone gets health care paid for or guaranteed by the state, usually through taxes.
statements.disagree: Health care is mainly bought privately or through insurance, with the state covering less.
statements.note: About how far the state should guarantee basic services.

statements.text: The minimum wage should be raised substantially.
statements.agree: The legal lowest wage goes up a lot, even if some employers have to pay more.
statements.disagree: Wages are left mostly to employers, workers and unions, or raised only slowly.
statements.note: About how much the state should set pay.

statements.text: Free markets allocate resources better than governments do.
statements.agree: Prices and competition generally decide better than officials what gets made and who gets it.
statements.disagree: Governments or public planning often decide better than markets what society needs.
statements.note: A core economic question: markets or the state.

statements.text: Major industries like energy, rail and utilities should be publicly owned.
statements.agree: Key industries are run by the state or public bodies instead of private companies.
statements.disagree: Those industries stay mostly in private hands, perhaps with regulation.
statements.note: About who owns the commanding heights of the economy.

statements.text: Taxes on the wealthy should be significantly higher.
statements.agree: High earners and the very rich pay a noticeably larger share in tax.
statements.disagree: Taxes on the wealthy stay as they are or go down.

statements.text: Labor unions are good for workers and for society.
statements.agree: Workers organizing collectively improves pay, conditions and fairness overall.
statements.disagree: Unions mostly protect insiders, raise costs or hold back the economy.

statements.text: Private property is a fundamental right that should be very hard to override.
statements.agree: Owners' rights to their property should almost never be overridden, even for public goals.
statements.disagree: Property can be limited, taxed or redistributed when the community needs it.
statements.note: About how absolute property rights are.

statements.text: Corporations should be more tightly regulated.
statements.agree: Companies face more rules on things like pollution, prices, labor and competition.
statements.disagree: Companies face fewer rules, or the current amount is enough.
statements.note: About the state's oversight of business.

statements.text: Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.
statements.agree: Benefits often discourage work and should be reduced.
statements.disagree: Welfare is a safety net worth keeping or expanding.
statements.note: About the size of the welfare state.

statements.text: Workers should collectively own the businesses they work in.
statements.agree: Businesses should belong to the people who work in them, for example as cooperatives.
statements.disagree: Businesses can be owned by investors, founders or the state as they are now.

statements.text: Government surveillance is acceptable if it prevents terrorism.
statements.agree: Security agencies may monitor communications if it helps stop attacks.
statements.disagree: Privacy should be protected even if it makes security work harder.

statements.text: Recreational drugs should be legal for adults.
statements.agree: Adults may legally buy and use drugs such as cannabis, possibly with regulation.
statements.disagree: Recreational drugs stay illegal.
statements.note: About personal freedom versus protection from harm.

statements.text: Hate speech should be legally restricted.
statements.agree: Speech that attacks groups for who they are can be punished by law.
statements.disagree: Offensive speech stays legal; it is answered with more speech, not law.

statements.text: A strong leader who can bypass political gridlock would benefit the country.
statements.agree: A decisive leader who can act without parliament or courts slowing things down would help.
statements.disagree: Checks and balances matter even when they slow decisions down.

statements.text: The state itself is unnecessary and harmful.
statements.agree: Society would be better off without governments at all.
statements.disagree: Some form of state is needed, whatever its size.

statements.text: Gun ownership should be strictly limited.
statements.agree: Owning guns requires strict licensing, or most private gun ownership is banned.
statements.disagree: Adults should be able to own guns with few restrictions.
statements.note: About gun rights versus gun control.

statements.text: The police and military need more funding and authority.
statements.agree: Police and armed forces get bigger budgets and more powers.
statements.disagree: Police and military budgets and powers stay the same or shrink.

statements.text: Sex work between consenting adults should be legal.
statements.agree: Adults can legally sell sexual services, ideally with rules for safety.
statements.disagree: Selling or buying sex should be banned or discouraged by law.
statements.note: About personal freedom, morality and exploitation.

statements.text: Decisions should be made as locally as possible rather than by national government.
statements.agree: Towns and regions make most decisions rather than the national government.
statements.disagree: National government sets common rules so the same standards apply everywhere.

statements.text: Prisons should focus on rehabilitation rather than punishment.
statements.agree: Prisons mainly try to help offenders change and return to society.
statements.disagree: Prisons mainly exist to punish and to protect the public.
statements.note: About the purpose of criminal justice.

statements.text: Traditional family structures are the foundation of a healthy society.
statements.agree: A married mother and father raising children is the model society should support.
statements.disagree: Many family forms are equally valid and none should be favored.

statements.text: Same-sex marriage should be legal.
statements.agree: Same-sex couples can marry with the same rights as anyone else.
statements.disagree: Marriage should be only between a man and a woman.

statements.text: Abortion should be legal in most cases.
statements.agree: Women can legally choose to end most pregnancies.
statements.disagree: Abortion should be banned or allowed only in rare cases.
statements.note: About reproductive rights and the status of the unborn.

statements.text: Religion should play a larger role in public life.
statements.agree: Religious values and institutions should shape laws, schools and public life more.
statements.disagree: Religion should stay a private matter, out of government.

statements.text: Society should actively work to correct historical racial injustices.
statements.agree: Society should take active steps, such as targeted programs, to repair past discrimination.
statements.disagree: Government should treat everyone the same now, without remedies for the past.
statements.note: About how to deal with historical racism.

statements.text: Gender is primarily a social construct.
statements.agree: Ideas of what men and women are like come mostly from culture, not biology.
statements.disagree: Differences between men and women are mostly natural or biological.

statements.text: Preserving national culture and traditions is important.
statements.agree: Protecting the nation's language, customs and heritage matters.
statements.disagree: Culture should change freely; preserving it is not a political goal.

statements.text: Social change should be gradual and respect established institutions.
statements.agree: Reform should be slow and build on existing institutions.
statements.disagree: Big, fast changes are sometimes needed even if institutions are disrupted.
statements.note: About the pace of change: conservative or radical.

statements.text: Immigration levels should be reduced.
statements.agree: Fewer people should be allowed to move into the country.
statements.disagree: Immigration should stay at current levels or increase.

statements.text: International organizations like the UN should have more power.
statements.agree: Bodies like the UN should be able to make more binding decisions over countries.
statements.disagree: Nations should keep decisions in their own hands.

statements.text: Free trade benefits everyone in the long run.
statements.agree: Fewer tariffs and trade barriers make all countries better off over time.
statements.disagree: Free trade hurts some workers or countries badly, so trade should be managed.

statements.text: My country should put its own interests ahead of global cooperation.
statements.agree: Your country's own interests come before international agreements.
statements.disagree: Cooperation with other countries usually comes first.

statements.text: Military intervention abroad is sometimes necessary to protect human rights.
statements.agree: Using force abroad can be right to stop mass atrocities.
statements.disagree: Military intervention in other countries is wrong or does more harm than good.

statements.text: National borders should eventually be open.
statements.agree: In the long run people should be free to live and work in any country.
statements.disagree: Countries should always control who can enter.

statements.text: Economic growth should be limited to protect the environment.
statements.agree: Protecting nature can mean accepting less economic growth.
statements.disagree: Growth should continue; environmental problems can be solved alongside it.

statements.text: Climate change requires drastic government action.
statements.agree: Governments should act fast and hard on emissions, even at real cost.
statements.disagree: Climate policy should be modest, market-led, or not a priority.

statements.text: Technological progress will solve most of humanity's problems.
statements.agree: Science and technology will fix most of what goes wrong for people.
statements.disagree: Technology can't solve problems that are social, moral or political.

statements.text: Nuclear power should be expanded.
statements.agree: Build more nuclear power plants.
statements.disagree: Phase out or avoid nuclear power.
statements.note: About energy policy; splits even environmentalists.

statements.text: Revolution is sometimes justified to achieve political change.
statements.agree: Overthrowing a government by force can sometimes be right.
statements.disagree: Change should only come through legal, peaceful means.

statements.text: Experts should have more say in policy than the general public.
statements.agree: Specialists should have more weight in decisions than public opinion.
statements.disagree: Ordinary people should have the final say, even against expert advice.

statements.text: A centrally planned economy can work better than a market economy.
statements.agree: A planned economy, where the state decides production, can outperform markets.
statements.disagree: Markets work better than central planning.
statements.note: Separates planned-economy socialism from other views.

statements.text: Markets are acceptable as long as businesses are owned by their workers or the public.
statements.agree: Firms can compete in markets as long as workers or the public own them.
statements.disagree: Markets are fine with private owners, or markets themselves are the problem.

statements.text: A tax on the value of land should replace most other taxes.
statements.agree: Taxing the value of land, not work or trade, should fund most of government.
statements.disagree: Keep taxing income, sales and other things as now.

statements.text: Large inheritances should be heavily taxed.
statements.agree: Big inheritances should be taxed heavily so wealth isn't simply passed down.
statements.disagree: People should be able to leave what they own to their family without heavy tax.

statements.text: Every adult should receive an unconditional basic income from the state.
statements.agree: Every adult gets a regular payment from the state, whether or not they work.
statements.disagree: Support should depend on need or on looking for work.

statements.text: Tariffs should protect domestic industry from foreign competition.
statements.agree: Taxes on imports should shield domestic producers from foreign competition.
statements.disagree: Imports should flow freely so consumers get the best price.

statements.text: The state should direct investment toward strategic industries.
statements.agree: The government should steer money into industries it considers important.
statements.disagree: Investors and markets should decide where money goes.

statements.text: Property should be spread widely among small owners rather than concentrated in corporations or the state.
statements.agree: Most people should own some land, a shop or a small business.
statements.disagree: Ownership by large firms or the state is fine.

statements.text: Money and wage labor should eventually be abolished.
statements.agree: Eventually people should work and share without money or wages.
statements.disagree: Money and wages are a normal, lasting part of society.

statements.text: Central banks should be abolished and money left to the market.
statements.agree: End central banks and let private money or free banking take over.
statements.disagree: Central banks should keep managing money and interest rates.
statements.note: About monetary policy; identifies some libertarians.

statements.text: Employers and workers should be organized into state-recognized bodies that set wages and prices together.
statements.agree: Officially recognized bodies of employers and workers should set wages and prices together.
statements.disagree: Wages and prices should come from markets or from independent unions.

statements.text: A single party guided by the correct ideology should lead the state.
statements.agree: One party with the right ideology should govern without rival parties.
statements.disagree: Several parties should compete for power.

statements.text: A hereditary monarch can be a legitimate and good head of state.
statements.agree: A king or queen who inherits the role can be a good head of state.
statements.disagree: Heads of state should be chosen, not inherited.

statements.text: Democracy is the best form of government, even when voters choose badly.
statements.agree: Democracy is best even when voters make poor choices.
statements.disagree: Other systems can be better than democracy.

statements.text: Citizens should vote directly on major laws rather than leaving them to representatives.
statements.agree: Citizens should decide major laws themselves through referendums.
statements.disagree: Elected representatives should make the laws.

statements.text: Workers' councils, not parliaments, should be the basis of political power.
statements.agree: Power should come from councils elected in workplaces, not from parliaments.
statements.disagree: Parliaments or other institutions should hold political power.
statements.note: Identifies council communism and some socialists.

statements.text: Regions should have the right to secede from the country.
statements.agree: Regions should be able to vote to leave the country.
statements.disagree: The country should stay whole; regions can't simply leave.

statements.text: Some people are naturally better suited to rule than others.
statements.agree: Some people are better suited by nature to govern.
statements.disagree: Everyone has an equal claim to take part in ruling.

statements.text: Political violence is never justified.
statements.agree: Violence is never an acceptable way to pursue political goals.
statements.disagree: Violence can sometimes be justified politically, for example against oppression.

statements.text: War can strengthen a nation's character.
statements.agree: Fighting wars can make a nation stronger and more united.
statements.disagree: War is a disaster that does not ennoble anyone.

statements.text: Religion and the state should be strictly separated.
statements.agree: Religion and government should have nothing to do with each other.
statements.disagree: Religion and state may be connected, for example through an official church.

statements.text: Laws should be based on religious scripture.
statements.agree: Laws should follow religious texts.
statements.disagree: Laws should be made by people, not drawn from scripture.

statements.text: Courts, policing and defense could be provided by private companies.
statements.agree: Security and justice could be bought from competing private providers.
statements.disagree: Courts, police and defense must be public.

statements.text: My country should maintain military superiority over its rivals.
statements.agree: Your country should be militarily stronger than its rivals.
statements.disagree: Military balance or cooperation matters more than superiority.

statements.text: A nation should be made up mainly of one ethnic group.
statements.agree: A nation should be mainly one ethnic people.
statements.disagree: A nation can include people of any ethnic background.

statements.text: Class conflict is the main driving force of history.
statements.agree: History is mainly driven by conflict between economic classes.
statements.disagree: Ideas, culture, individuals or other forces matter more than class conflict.

statements.text: Society should aim for equality of outcomes, not only of opportunity.
statements.agree: Society should aim for people to end up with similar levels of wealth and well-being.
statements.disagree: Equal chances matter; different results are acceptable.

statements.text: Indigenous peoples should have authority over their traditional lands.
statements.agree: Indigenous peoples should control their traditional territories.
statements.disagree: Those lands should be governed like the rest of the country.

statements.text: Former colonial powers owe reparations to the nations they colonized.
statements.agree: Countries that had colonies should compensate the countries they colonized.
statements.disagree: Reparations for colonialism are not owed or not workable.

statements.text: Nations that share a religion or civilization should unite politically.
statements.agree: Countries with a shared religion or civilization should join politically.
statements.disagree: Countries should stay separate, or unite on other grounds.
statements.note: Identifies pan-Islamism, Eurasianism and similar movements.

statements.text: Pursuing your own self-interest is morally good.
statements.agree: Looking after your own interests is right, not just allowed.
statements.disagree: Concern for others should come before self-interest.

statements.text: Citizens' duties to their community come before their individual rights.
statements.agree: What you owe your community matters more than your personal rights.
statements.disagree: Individual rights come first.

statements.text: Nature has value in itself, apart from its usefulness to humans.
statements.agree: Nature matters for its own sake, not only because it is useful to people.
statements.disagree: Nature matters because of what it does for humans.

statements.text: Population growth should be actively limited.
statements.agree: Governments should actively slow population growth.
statements.disagree: Population size should not be controlled by the state.

statements.text: Industrial civilization has been a disaster for humanity.
statements.agree: Industrial society has done more harm than good to humanity.
statements.disagree: Industrialization has been a great improvement for people.

statements.text: Society should speed up technological change even if it disrupts existing institutions.
statements.agree: Speed up technological change even if it upends existing institutions.
statements.disagree: Slow down or manage technological change to protect society.

statements.text: People should be free to enhance their bodies and minds with technology.
statements.agree: People may use technology to improve their bodies and minds.
statements.disagree: Human nature should not be altered with technology.

statements.text: AI and algorithms should take over more government decision-making.
statements.agree: Let AI and algorithms make more public decisions.
statements.disagree: Keep public decisions with humans.

statements.text: People should be able to use encryption the government cannot break.
statements.agree: People should be able to keep their communications private, even from government.
statements.disagree: Authorities should be able to access encrypted data with a warrant.

statements.text: Restoring a lost social order matters more than pursuing progress.
statements.agree: Recovering how society used to be matters more than moving forward.
statements.disagree: Progress matters more than restoring the past.

statements.text: Policies should be judged by their results, not by whether they fit an ideology.
statements.agree: Use whatever works, regardless of which ideology it comes from.
statements.disagree: Principles matter even when other policies might work better.
